newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto said in fighting mood after dismissal.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto said in fighting mood after dismissal.

text.p: Aides to Pakistan's ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto said on Tuesday she was in high spirits and ready to fight her dismissal by President Farooq Leghari.
But the 43-year-old leader spent her first day out of office as a virtual prisoner at her official home in Islamabad, guarded by troops who barred her former ministers from meeting her.
There was no official word on Bhutto's status, but lawyers for her ex-defence minister filed a court petition claiming that she had been illegally detained, court sources said.

By Tuesday evening, a provincial chief minister from Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) was the only outsider known to have been allowed to meet her, but an aide who talked to her by telephone said she was in high spirits.
Both described Bhutto as a "fighter", hinting she would not meekly accept the latest blow in her chequered political career.
Lawyers acting for dismissed defence minister Aftab Shaaban Meerani filed the habeas corpus petition for Bhutto before the Lahore High Court's bench in Rawalpindi city, near Islamabad.
The court issued a notice to the secretary of the Interior Ministry and set the hearing for Wednesday, court sources said.
Bhutto was held virtually incommunicado at her house after Leghari issued a proclamation dismissing her in the early hours.
Troops allowed the chief minister of North West Frontier Province, Aftab Sherpao, to visit her in the afternoon. He was the first Bhutto loyalist known to have gained access to her.
Sherpao earlier visited Leghari, who had also dissolved the National Assembly (lower house) and appointed a caretaker premier to oversee snap elections on February 3, 1997.

Former government ministers who tried to see Bhutto earlier in the day said they were turned back by police posted near her residence, an elegant white two-storey house on a low hill overlooking a sprawl of government buildings.
"She was in high spirits and will soon be meeting the party leaders to chalk out the future strategy," the official APP news agency quoted Sherpao as saying after meeting Bhutto.
Asked about Bhutto's response to her dismissal, he said: "She reacted in a manner as an elected leader should in such circumstances," but did not elaborate.

"She is in high spirits and you know she is a fighter," Bhutto's political secretary Naheed Khan told reporters after army officers allowed her to talk to her leader by telephone from a security cabin at a gate outside the prime minister's house. "And God willing we will fight it out."
The PPP has called a meeting of its central executive committee for Wednesday to chart its strategy, and Naheed said Bhutto would preside over it if allowed to do so.
She said she hoped Bhutto would be able to meet people she had named on a list submitted to the presidency for clearance.

Naheed said Bhutto's mother Nusrat and three children were with her at her residence. Her husband, sacked investment minister Asif Ali Zardari, was detained by troops early on Tuesday in the Punjab provincial capital of Lahore.
